stories.headline: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from crypto exchange Binance in massive cyber heist
stories.body:
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from cryptocurrency exchange Binance in a record cyber heist. The company froze around half of the stolen funds after the attack occurred. Binance secured $3 billion of its stolen digital assets. Unidentified hackers held the remaining funds.

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM reported that an attacker moved about $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets. The funds were moved across ten blockchains, mostly within 20 minutes. NyxLab CEO Kok Tin Gan said the attack appeared to involve one signature. That signature granted a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said hackers used a self-destruct mechanism. The mechanism destroyed tooling and traces as they went. Analytics firms linked the Binance hack to a North Korean hacking unit. Experts including TRM Labs attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean unit also called Lazarus Group. Chainalysis co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin said on X that the group likely did the attack.

Cryptocurrency theft generates an estimated half of North Korea's foreign currency income. A UN panel of experts reported in spring 2024 that it was reviewing 58 suspected North Korean cyber-attacks. Those attacks targeted cryptocurrency companies between 2017 and 2023, and they were worth $3 billion. In February 2016, North Korean hackers tried to move $951 million from Bangladesh Bank's account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. They ultimately stole $81 million in that attack.

The Binance heist eclipsed a $1.5 billion hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025. Binance set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the stolen assets. The US Secret Service said it was working around the clock to identify, freeze, trace, and recover stolen funds. The price of Bitcoin fell 5% to $76,800 in Friday afternoon trading in New York after news of the hack.

Binance was founded in China in 2017. It has an estimated total of over 300 million registered users worldwide. Former Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty in 2023 to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform. US President Donald Trump pardoned Zhao in 2025.

stories.headline: Israeli general election ends in deadlock as Benjamin Netanyahu falls short of majority
stories.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed to win a parliamentary majority in the national election. His Likud party won 27 seats, remaining the largest party in the Knesset. But his right-wing coalition won 53 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority. A rival bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats.

Netanyahu accused Palestinian Israeli parties of stealing the election and receiving money from Qatar. Israel's Electoral Commission found no evidence of fraud regarding Palestinian Israeli parties. Qatar also denied involvement. Acting Central Elections Committee Director General Dean Livne said there was no basis for allegations of systematic violations. Israeli security agency Shin Bet investigated whether Arab-led parties received illegal foreign funding from Qatar and Turkey.

Arab Israelis make up about one-fifth of Israel's population. The Arab party lists The Joint List and Ra'am won a record 19 seats following high turnout. US President Donald Trump endorsed Netanyahu before the election. In Israel, a candidate given a mandate to form a government has 28 days to get support from 61 lawmakers, with a possible 14-day extension.

Israel's Electoral Commission found no evidence of fraud regarding Palestinian Israeli parties, and Qatar denied involvement.

stories.headline: Civilians leave Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare localized ceasefire
stories.body:
Hundreds of residents left the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky during a four-hour ceasefire on Friday. US First Lady Melania Trump brokered the localized humanitarian ceasefire in the city. The population of Oleshky fell from a pre-war total of 24,000 to about 2,000.

Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia said evacuated residents traveled to Anapa in Russia. From there, they will fly to Belarus and travel by bus to Ukraine. Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said 25 buses and nine ambulances helped with evacuations. The ceasefire allowed workers to de-mine roads leading out of Oleshky.

Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said this was the first long frontline ceasefire maintained since 2022. The Kremlin described the Oleshky ceasefire as a special case that is hard to apply to broader peace talks. Russian forces captured Oleshky in February 2022. The city suffered severe flooding after the Kakhovka dam was destroyed in June 2023. In another attack, a Russian drone strike on a train station in Dnipro killed at least 13 people on Thursday.

The Kremlin described the Oleshky ceasefire as a special case that was difficult to extrapolate to broader peace negotiations.
Oleshky was captured by Russian forces in February 2022 and suffered severe flooding following the destruction of the Kakhovka dam in June 2023.
A Russian drone strike on a train station in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro killed at least 13 people on Thursday.

stories.headline: Polish police enter Constitutional Tribunal as head judge faces suspension
stories.body:
Polish police entered the Constitutional Tribunal building in Warsaw after demonstrators threw objects at officers. Demonstrators gathered outside the court during the protest. Supporters of the opposition Law and Justice party chanted that Tusk was a traitor and prayed outside.

Authorities suspended Constitutional Tribunal head Bogdan Swieczkowski. He had used his power to block judges elected by the parliamentary majority from working. Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek requested that legal immunity be removed for Swieczkowski and his deputy so they could face criminal charges. Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska was put in charge of the court after the suspension.

The Constitutional Court stated on social media that the actions against its top judges were a coup. It insisted that the judges remain legally appointed. Polish President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around while flying to Senegal. He said the president must be in Poland during the court crisis. Nawrocki has refused to swear in five court judges elected by parliament since March. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said restoring the rule of law after years of Law and Justice party lawlessness is a difficult process.

stories.headline: ISRO successfully launches NVS-03 navigation satellite aboard GSLV-F18 rocket
stories.body:
The Indian Space Research Organisation successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Friday. A GSLV-F18 rocket carried the satellite into space from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. Liftoff occurred at 11:51 pm Indian Standard Time on October 30, 2026, from the Second Launch Pad. The rocket measured 51.7 metres tall.

The GSLV-F18 rocket placed the 2,250 kg NVS-03 satellite into geosynchronous transfer orbit 18 minutes after liftoff. ISRO accomplished the GSLV-F18 mission with a turnaround time of 56 days after the earlier GSLV-F17 mission.

ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan stated that the mission restored the NavIC constellation to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites. NavIC was originally designed with a constellation of seven satellites placed in geostationary and geosynchronous orbits. But the last functioning atomic clock aboard the IRNSS-1F satellite stopped working on March 13, 2026. That left only three operational satellites in the NavIC system.

India's armed forces rely on foreign navigation systems like US GPS and Russian GLONASS when NavIC has fewer than four operational satellites. The success of NVS-03 restores that minimum requirement. The replacement satellite NVS-02 failed to reach its intended orbit on January 29, 2025, because of a pyro valve signal loss in its engine. For this launch, ISRO kept specific valves open before liftoff to prevent the same technical problem from happening again.

The NVS-03 satellite carries an indigenously manufactured atomic clock alongside imported atomic clocks. The satellite transmits signals in the L1, L5, and S bands. These signals make NavIC compatible with modern civilian smartphone chipsets. In June 2025, the Indian government announced plans to replace US GPS with five atomic clocks located across India to maintain Indian Standard Time.

stories.headline: Oil tankers carrying Indian seafarers targeted in Strait of Hormuz attacks
stories.body:
Explosive devices damaged an oil tanker carrying Indian seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday. The Panama-flagged oil tanker MT Louise 1 was carrying 27 Indian seafarers when it was targeted with limpet mines. The attack damaged the ship's engine room and temporarily disabled the vessel before crew members controlled an onboard fire.

On October 29, the Liberia-flagged MT Arzanah was hit in a projectile attack in the Strait of Hormuz while carrying two Indian nationals. Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that all 29 Indian seafarers across both ships were safe. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar raised concerns about attacks on civilian shipping during the G20 foreign ministers' meeting on Friday.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a small boat attached explosive devices to a tanker on Friday. Limpet mines attach to a ship's hull using magnets to damage machinery. Meanwhile, the Omani Maritime Security Centre evacuated 25 crew members from the burning Panamanian-flagged oil tanker RITI on Friday. December Brent crude futures rose $2.76, or 2.4 percent, to settle at $117.64 a barrel on Friday.
